html:
The Eswatini protests of 2021 were a wave of demonstrations for democracy that peaked in late June and July 2021, when protesters in Manzini and Mbabane were shot by security forces.

Anger at the absolute rule of Mswati III, poverty and the death of a student in police custody set off protests. When marchers tried to deliver petitions for an elected prime minister, the government banned them. Shops and buildings linked to the king were burned, and soldiers were deployed.

Dozens of people were killed. Two members of parliament who backed reform were later jailed. The protests failed to change the system, but they showed deep discontent in Eswatini and drew regional mediation, against a monarchy built by Sobhuza II.
sum: The Eswatini protests of 2021 were a wave of demonstrations for democracy that peaked in late June and July 2021, when protesters in Manzini and Mbabane were shot by security forces.
